sounder.title: Sounder
sounder.summary: A poor Black sharecropper family struggles to find enough food, and the father is arrested after taking a ham. The unnamed boy searches for his injured dog and later goes looking for his father, hungering to learn to read along the way.
sounder.setting: Rural American South (Georgia counties mentioned; place never named), before the mid-1950s
sounder.note: Setting corrected: not explicitly Depression-era or 19th century; only the dog is named in the book.

the-arkadians.title: The Arkadians
the-arkadians.summary: Lucian, a palace bean-counter, flees after uncovering fraud among the royal soothsayers. He joins a mysterious girl with strange powers and a poet turned into a donkey, and they set out to restore the poet to human form.
characters: Fronto, a poet turned into a donkey
Joy-in-the-Dance, a mysterious girl with strange powers
the-arkadians.setting: Arkadia, a land drawn from Greek myth
the-arkadians.note: Corrected Lucian from lawyer's assistant to palace bean-counter; Fronto is a poet turned donkey.

the-bears-house.title: The Bears' House
the-bears-house.summary: Fran Ellen and her brother Fletcher hide from welfare workers and teachers after their father leaves and their mother falls too ill to care for the family. Fran Ellen finds comfort in a bear family living in a doll's house at school.
characters: The bear family in the doll's house
the-bears-house.note: City not named in the page read; San Francisco setting unverified so removed. ALA Notable claim comes from a search snippet.

the-black-stallion-and-satan.title: The Black Stallion and Satan
the-black-stallion-and-satan.summary: Alec Ramsay inherits the Black, and a question arises of whether the Black or his colt Satan is faster. A raging forest fire puts both horses in a race for their lives.
the-black-stallion-and-satan.note: Series is the numbered Black Stallion books (1941-1983); this is #5. Illustrator unverified so null. Plot detail from search snippet only.

the-changeling.title: The Changeling
the-changeling.summary: Shy, anxious Martha befriends fearless, imaginative Ivy Carson, who calls herself a changeling. Together they build a make-believe world, the Land of the Green Sky, and their friendship is shaped by growing up.
the-changeling.setting: A town and the hills above it with the Carson family's derelict mansion
the-changeling.note: Source URL fixed (disambiguated title); added illustrator and awards; California 1950s unverified so removed.

the-dark-is-rising.title: The Dark Is Rising
the-dark-is-rising.summary: On his eleventh birthday at midwinter, Will Stanton discovers he is one of the Old Ones, who serve the Light against the Dark. He must gather the Signs to help the Light as magic stirs through the Christmas season.
the-dark-is-rising.setting: Thames Valley, England, from the winter solstice to Twelfth Night
the-dark-is-rising.note: Added illustrator; Rider/Merriman details unverified beyond series knowledge, so Rider removed.

the-devil-s-other-storybook.title: The Devil's Other Storybook
the-devil-s-other-storybook.summary: Ten more tales about the Devil, mostly set in the afterlife, where a lazy Satan dispenses poetic rather than gruesome justice. Witty and good for reading aloud.
the-devil-s-other-storybook.note: Collection has ten stories; age 8-12 per Publishers Weekly (search snippet).

the-fledgling.title: The Fledgling
the-fledgling.summary: Georgie Dorian believes she can fly and is taught by a Canada goose called the Goose Prince. A hunter obsessed with the bird threatens them in Concord.
the-fledgling.note: Corrected heroine surname to Dorian and goose to Goose Prince; illustrator unverified so null.

the-green-book.title: The Green Book
the-green-book.summary: As Earth dies, a group of refugees including a girl named Pattie flee in an old spaceship to a new planet. The colony struggles to survive there.
the-green-book.note: First published London 1981 (Macmillan); US edition 1982 illustrated by Lloyd Bloom; reissued as Shine (1988). Plot details from search snippets.

the-high-king.title: The High King
the-high-king.summary: War engulfs Prydain as Arawn's forces strike, and Taran and his companions rally the land against him. It concludes the Chronicles of Prydain.
the-high-king.note: Doli removed from main characters; summary rewritten to remove Dyrnwyn-delivery detail.

the-night-journey.title: The Night Journey
the-night-journey.summary: Rachel overhears her great-grandmother Nana Sashie telling of her childhood escape from Russia. The story recounts flight from pogroms in the Russian Empire.
the-night-journey.setting: Mykolaiv in the Russian Empire, early 1900s; later Minnesota
the-night-journey.note: Award year corrected to 1982; added illustrator; Association of Jewish Libraries Award from catalog snippet.

the-pearl.title: The Pearl
the-pearl.summary: A poor pearl diver in a Mexican fishing village finds a huge pearl and hopes it will change his family's life. Instead it draws greed and danger toward them.
the-pearl.setting: La Paz, Baja California Sur, Mexico, 1940s
the-pearl.note: Setting period adjusted; first appeared as short story in 1945.

the-story-of-siegfried.title: The Story of Siegfried
the-story-of-siegfried.summary: A retelling of the Norse and German legends of Siegfried, from his boyhood apprenticeship to the smith Mimer to his meeting with a dragon and cursed treasure.
the-story-of-siegfried.note: Author is the Indiana educator James Baldwin (1841-1925), not the civil rights writer. Brunhild removed (unverified); illustrator unverified (Howard Pyle named in search results for editions) so null.

the-transfigured-hart.title: The Transfigured Hart
the-transfigured-hart.summary: A boy and a girl encounter an albino deer in the woods that on one special night becomes a unicorn.
awards: Golden Kite Honor Book 1974 (as listed by author site)
the-transfigured-hart.note: Award is Golden Kite Honor, not winner; names Richard/Heather unverified so removed; setting unverified so null.

the-tunnel-of-hugsy-goode.title: The Tunnel of Hugsy Goode
the-tunnel-of-hugsy-goode.summary: Nobody believed Hugsy Goode's claim of a tunnel under the alley. Years later two boys, Nicholas and Timothy, find an entrance and explore it.
the-tunnel-of-hugsy-goode.setting: An alley near the old Goode house, with a tunnel beneath it
the-tunnel-of-hugsy-goode.note: Boys are Nicholas and Timothy, not Jerry; the Cranbury setting claim removed.

the-van-gogh-cafe.title: The Van Gogh Cafe
the-van-gogh-cafe.summary: A cafe in Flowers, Kansas becomes a place of strange magic after a lightning strike. Linked episodes follow Marc, the owner, his 10-year-old daughter Clara, and visitors.
the-van-gogh-cafe.note: Illustrator Rylant not confirmed so null; character Doll removed.

the-winged-watchman.title: The Winged Watchman
the-winged-watchman.summary: A Dutch family and their windmill during the German occupation of the Netherlands in World War II. Windmill arm positions are used to signal the resistance.
the-winged-watchman.note: Newbery Honor 1963 removed: van Stockum's only Newbery Honor was 1935 for A Day on Skates. Sheltering a Jewish child unverified, removed.

the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz.summary: A tornado carries Dorothy and Toto from Kansas to Oz. She follows the Yellow Brick Road to the Emerald City with a Scarecrow, Tin Woodman and Cowardly Lion to ask the Wizard for help.
the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz.setting: Kansas and the Land of Oz
the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz.note: Source was a 404; first published Sept 1, 1900 per Wikipedia (May 17 elsewhere).

tuck-everlasting.title: Tuck Everlasting
tuck-everlasting.summary: Ten-year-old Winnie Foster discovers the Tuck family, who gained immortality from a spring in the woods. A stranger wants to exploit the water, and Winnie must choose what to do.
characters: The Man in the Yellow Suit
tuck-everlasting.note: Setting 1880 village Treegap, not generic New England; awards added.

unreal-eight-surprising-stories.title: Unreal! Eight Surprising Stories
unreal-eight-surprising-stories.summary: Eight funny, odd stories with twist endings, including Without a Shirt, Skeleton on the Dunny and Wunderpants. Several became episodes of the TV series Round the Twist.
unreal-eight-surprising-stories.series: Paul Jennings short story collections #1 (Unbelievable! 1986 follows)
unreal-eight-surprising-stories.note: Awards added; source fixed from author page to collection article.

white-stallion-of-lipizza.title: White Stallion of Lipizza
white-stallion-of-lipizza.summary: Hans, a baker's son in Vienna, dreams of working with the Lipizzan stallions of the Spanish Riding School. The book follows him and his horse Borina through training.
white-stallion-of-lipizza.note: Published by Rand McNally 1964; Borina is the stallion.

Robert Lawson.bio: Robert Lawson was an American author, illustrator and etcher. He illustrated The Story of Ferdinand and Mr. Popper's Penguins and wrote his own books. He is the only person to win both the Caldecott (1941) and Newbery (1945) Medals.

Will James.bio: Born Joseph Ernest Nephtali Dufault, he became a cowboy artist and writer and claimed a Montana birth. He won the 1927 Newbery Medal for Smoky the Cowhorse.

William H. Armstrong.bio: Armstrong taught history at Kent School in Connecticut for 52 years and wrote children's books. Sounder won the 1970 Newbery Medal.

Charles G. Waugh.bio: American college professor and anthologist who co-edited many anthologies, mostly with Martin H. Greenberg and Isaac Asimov.
known_for: Anthologies with Isaac Asimov and Martin H. Greenberg

Marion Smoothey.bio: Author of children's mathematics nonfiction in the Let's Investigate series; no personal details found.
